title: Independent prediction in sustained higher Reynolds number turbulence
status: Calibration design; models must be frozen before any test simulation

response_pilot.description: Completed long-run screening field, with separate base, half-step and fine-grid responses; outside all prediction splits

inference.target: Integral from 0 to 1.5 of E_delta(t)/E_delta(0), model time units
inference.unit: One independently initialized baseline run, with all four times and both strengths kept together
inference.primary: Mean run RMSE of history minus richer present model; paired 95% run bootstrap
inference.support: Require upper 95% difference limits below zero against richer present, global present, wrong-run history expectation, strength prior, and event-strength prior, AND all stationarity/numerical gates. This is a joint intersection-union claim; individual comparisons are not simultaneous intervals.
inference.null: Three models trained with whole-run history derangements. Average run RMSE over every different test-run donor; resample run nodes in both roles, excluding equal original seeds.
inference.limitation: Conditional on one calibration ensemble and candidate model family. This does not prove physical memory beyond the complete current field, high-Reynolds asymptotic universality, or marker-history prediction.

refinement_design: Four predeclared test runs. Restart both controls from each base checkpoint at event minus 2. Half uses n64 and half of both steps; fine uses n80 and those same smaller steps. Compare half-base for time and fine-half for space. Full long-run pilots are separate statistical checks.

sources.title: Energy transfer and dissipation in forced isotropic turbulence
